measured: the applications twin-world's demand scan reads (demand/applications.json; Runhuman 1 is not read), each at the commit the scan cloned (generated/demand.json scanned, ~/.cache/twin-demand), read for the openai SDK's calls, the AI SDK's OpenAI provider (whose model call is the Responses API from @ai-sdk/openai 2), LangChain's and CopilotKit's OpenAI clients, and every api.openai.com URL, each call mapped to the published document's operation. Only what the running product calls counts: tests, fixtures, lab and probe scripts, egress allow lists and a JWT claim's name are not demand. Outside the demand: Twenty's transcription model factory, which no code at 1d561b8c calls; LibreChat's openai.beta.assistants.files (v1 Assistants' file attachments, a path absent from the published document). Supercode's Realtime voice is a WebSocket beside the HTTP document (the manifest's socket realtime, semantics/sockets.ts). Subscription source inventory: Codex 0.151.0 pinned by Browser Substrate, Open Autonomy’s installed 0.156.1 and Harness’s container 0.153.4, plus Hermes v2026.8.31 commit 29112bef099274229cadff79cdff7bf7b99c4b77. Those runtime paths enable sign-in, coding turns, model discovery and TUI account usage. The products do not enable Codex cloud task commands, remote control, marketplace plugin installation or experimental voice, so those separate client flows remain unmodeled. chat.openai.com is merely Substrate’s allowlist and the vendor’s legacy base normalization; no product dials it. JWT claim URLs are names, not outbound calls. All other Volter product clones, the platform and launch were searched before the ruling. Usage attribution: OA and RH2 getAuthStatus and codex-only forwarding do not read wham usage; Harness sign-in alone does not prove it. Substrate native interactive TUI prefetch is the concrete caller.
